name: list_all_authorizations
description:
List all connected (authorized) connectors for the current user.
Returns both Phoenix Server built-in connectors (Google, GitHub, Twitter, LinkedIn, Notion,
TikTok, CJ, Square) and Composio-managed connectors (Instagram, etc.).

Use this tool when the user asks about their connected/authorized apps or connectors,
e.g. "What connectors do I have?", "Which apps are connected?", "Show my authorizations".

Args:
    provider: Optional filter by provider name (e.g. "google", "composio", "figma", "higgsfield").

name: start_github_auth
description: Start GitHub OAuth authorization flow.

name: exchange_github_connector_code
description:
Exchange and store a GitHub OAuth code from the Phoenix PC local callback.

This tool is used when GitHub authorization redirects to the PC local gateway
instead of the MCP public callback. The MCP server performs the code exchange
and persists credentials in the same store used by normal GitHub callbacks.

name: manage_github_org_access
description:
Manage GitHub organization access for the connected OAuth App.

Use this tool when:
- The user recently joined a new GitHub organization and needs to grant
  the OAuth App access to it.
- An org-scoped operation (list org repos, create repo under org, fork
  to org) returns 403 because the OAuth App has not been granted access
  to that organization.
- The user wants to review or revoke organization-level access.

Re-running start_github_auth does NOT help here — GitHub skips the
organization selection screen when the user has already authorized the
app. This tool returns a direct link to the GitHub settings page where
the user can grant or revoke per-organization access.

name: create_github_repo
description:
Create a new GitHub repository, either under the authenticated user
or under a GitHub organization.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Create a new repo called my-project"
- "Help me set up a new private GitHub repository"
- "Initialize a new project on GitHub"
- "Create a repo named foo under the my-org organization"

Args:
    name: Repository name (required). Must be unique under the chosen
          owner (user or org). Example: "my-awesome-project".
    description: Short description of the repository.
    private: If True, create a private repo. Default False (public).
    auto_init: If True, initialize with a README. Default True.
    org: If provided, create the repo under this GitHub organization
         instead of the authenticated user's account. The authenticated
         user must have permission to create repositories in that org
         (org "Repository creation" policy + sufficient role). When
         omitted (default), the repo is created under the user's
         account — backward compatible.
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON with the created repo: full_name, html_url, private,
    description, default_branch, created_at.

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion. Common org
    failures: 403 (insufficient permission / org policy forbids creation),
    404 (org not found or not visible to the token), 422 (name already
    taken in the org).

name: fork_github_repo
description:
Fork an existing GitHub repository to the authenticated user's account.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Fork facebook/react to my account"
- "I want my own copy of this repo"
- "Fork this project to my org"

Args:
    owner: Owner of the repository to fork, e.g. "facebook".
    repo: Repository name to fork, e.g. "react".
    organization: If provided, fork to this org instead of the user's account.
                  The user must be a member of the org.
    name: Custom name for the forked repo. Default is the original repo name.
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON with the forked repo: full_name, html_url, private,
    description, parent (source repo full_name).

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: list_github_repos
description:
List GitHub repositories accessible to the authenticated user,
including **private repos** that are invisible without login.

By default, lists repos owned by / accessible to the authenticated user
(``GET /user/repos``). When ``organization`` is supplied, the tool
switches to listing repos under that organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``);
private repos the authenticated user has access to within the org are
included.

Note: this tool intentionally does NOT accept a ``username`` filter.
GitHub's ``GET /users/{username}/repos`` endpoint only ever returns
public repositories — even when authenticated and even when the
username matches the caller — so exposing it here would mislead users
into thinking private repos can be listed by username. To see your
own private repos, simply omit ``organization``.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "What repos do I have?"
- "Show me my private repositories"
- "List my recently updated projects"
- "Show all repositories under the alibaba organization"

Args:
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    visibility: Filter — "all" (default), "public", or "private".
        Only applies when listing the authenticated user's own repos
        (i.e. ``organization`` is not provided).
    sort: Sort field — "created", "updated" (default), "pushed", or "full_name".
    per_page: Results per page, 1–100. Default 20.
    page: Page number starting at 1.
    organization: If provided, list repositories under this GitHub
        organization (``GET /orgs/{org}/repos``).

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ repos: [...], pagination: {...}, user_login,
    scope: {...} }``. ``scope`` describes which listing was performed:
    ``{"type": "self" | "org", "target": <name or null>}``.
    Each repo: full_name, description, html_url, private, language,
    stargazers_count, forks_count, updated_at, default_branch.

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: star_github_repo
description:
Star a GitHub repository as the authenticated user.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Star this repo"
- "Add facebook/react to my stars"
- "Bookmark this project"

Args:
    owner: Repository owner, e.g. "facebook".
    repo: Repository name, e.g. "react".
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ starred: true, repo: "owner/repo" }``

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: unstar_github_repo
description:
Unstar a GitHub repository as the authenticated user.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "Unstar this repo"
- "Remove facebook/react from my stars"

Args:
    owner: Repository owner, e.g. "facebook".
    repo: Repository name, e.g. "react".
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ unstarred: true, repo: "owner/repo" }``

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: list_github_starred
description:
List repositories that the authenticated user has starred.

This is the user's personal bookmark / collection list on GitHub.

Call this tool when the user asks:
- "What repos have I starred?"
- "Show my GitHub stars"
- "What projects did I bookmark?"

Args:
    user_login: GitHub username whose credential to use. Leave empty to auto-detect.
    sort: Sort field — "created" (default, when you starred it) or "updated".
    direction: Sort direction — "desc" (default, newest first) or "asc".
    per_page: Results per page, 1–100. Default 20.
    page: Page number starting at 1.

Returns:
    On success — JSON ``{ starred_repos: [...], pagination: {...}, user_login }``
    Each repo: full_name, description, html_url, private, language,
    stargazers_count, forks_count, updated_at, default_branch.

    On failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: list_github_issues
description:
List GitHub issues (search-backed; cross-repo or scoped).

`filter` is **scope-aware** when omitted: with `owner`/`repo`/`org` it
defaults to `"none"` (all items in that scope); without scope it defaults
to `"assigned"` (the user's personal dashboard). For when-to-use guidance,
user-wording → `filter` mapping, and pagination caveats, see SKILL.md
`github-tools` (Pitfalls 3, 4, 6).

Args:
    filter: One of `"assigned"` / `"authored"` / `"mentioned"` / `"none"`.
        Leave unset for the scope-aware default. `"none"` requires
        `owner`/`repo`/`org`.
    state: `"open"` (default) / `"closed"` / `"all"`. Case-insensitive.
    owner: Repo owner OR user/org login. With `repo` → single repo;
        alone → `user:owner` (all repos of that owner).
    repo: Repo name; requires `owner`.
    org: Limit to repos owned by this org (`org:` qualifier).
    labels: Comma-separated labels, e.g. `"bug,help wanted"`.
    sort: `"created"` / `"updated"` (default) / `"comments"`. Descending only.
    per_page: 1–100, default 20.
    page: 1-based. GitHub caps search at 1000 results total.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON `{ issues: [...], pagination: {page, per_page, returned,
    total_count, incomplete_results}, query, user_login }`. Each issue:
    number, title, state, user, assignees, html_url, comments, labels,
    created_at, updated_at. `assignees` is a list of login strings (empty
    when no one is assigned).

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: list_github_pull_requests
description:
List GitHub pull requests (search-backed; cross-repo or scoped).

`filter` is **scope-aware** when omitted: with `owner`/`repo`/`org` it
defaults to `"none"` (all items in that scope); without scope it defaults
to `"review_requested"` (PRs awaiting the user's review). Branch filtering
(`head` / `base`) is not exposed. For when-to-use guidance, user-wording
→ `filter` mapping, and pagination caveats, see SKILL.md `github-tools`
(Pitfalls 3, 4, 6).

Args:
    filter: One of `"review_requested"` / `"reviewed_by"` / `"authored"`
        / `"assigned"` / `"mentioned"` / `"none"`. Leave unset for the
        scope-aware default. `"none"` requires `owner`/`repo`/`org`.
    state: `"open"` (default) / `"closed"` / `"all"`. Case-insensitive.
    owner / repo / org / labels: Same semantics as `list_github_issues`.
    sort: `"created"` / `"updated"` (default) / `"comments"`. Descending only.
    per_page: 1–100, default 20.
    page: 1-based. GitHub caps search at 1000 results total.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON `{ pull_requests: [...], pagination: {page, per_page,
    returned, total_count, incomplete_results}, query, user_login }`.
    Each PR: number, title, state, draft, user, assignees, html_url,
    head, base, created_at, updated_at. `assignees` is a list of login
    strings (empty when no one is assigned). For requested reviewers,
    use `get_github_pull_request_content`. (`head`/`base` may be null
    on search results.)

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: get_github_issue_content
description:
Drill into a single GitHub issue: body + metadata + first page of
comments. Pair with `list_github_issues` to discover `number`.

Args:
    owner: Repo owner, e.g. `"facebook"`.
    repo: Repo name, e.g. `"react"`.
    number: Issue number (the integer after `#`).
    include_comments: If True (default), also fetch the first page of
        conversation comments. Set False to save one API call when only
        the body is needed.
    comments_per_page: 1–100, default 30. Only the first page is fetched;
        inspect `pagination.has_more` and re-issue with paging if needed.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON `{ issue: {...}, comments: [...] | null, pagination:
    {comments_returned, comments_per_page, has_more}, user_login }`.

    Issue fields: number, title, state, state_reason, user, html_url,
    comments (count), labels, assignees, milestone, body, created_at,
    updated_at, closed_at.
    Comment: id, user, html_url, body, created_at, updated_at.

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: get_github_pull_request_content
description:
Drill into a single GitHub PR: body + merge state + diff stats + first
page of conversation comments + first page of line-level review comments.
Pair with `list_github_pull_requests` to discover `number`.

Note: returns diff *stats* (`additions`/`deletions`/`changed_files`), not
the file-by-file patch. For the patch, point the user at `html_url + ".diff"`.

Args:
    owner: Repo owner, e.g. `"facebook"`.
    repo: Repo name, e.g. `"react"`.
    number: PR number (the integer after `#`).
    include_comments: If True (default), fetch the first page of
        conversation comments (PR timeline).
    include_review_comments: If True (default), fetch the first page of
        line-level review comments anchored to the diff.
    comments_per_page: 1–100, default 30. Applies to both comment kinds;
        only one page is fetched per kind. `pagination.*_has_more` tells
        you whether to follow up.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON `{ pull_request: {...}, comments: [...] | null,
    review_comments: [...] | null, pagination: {comments_returned,
    review_comments_returned, comments_per_page, comments_has_more,
    review_comments_has_more}, user_login }`.

    PR fields: number, title, state, draft, user, html_url, head, base,
    labels, assignees, requested_reviewers, milestone, body, merged,
    mergeable, mergeable_state, merge_commit_sha, commits, additions,
    deletions, changed_files, review_comments (count), comments (count),
    created_at, updated_at, closed_at, merged_at.
    Comment: id, user, html_url, body, created_at, updated_at.
    Review comment additionally: path, line, side, start_line, start_side,
    commit_id, in_reply_to_id.

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: create_github_issue
description:
Create a new GitHub issue in the given repository.

Use this for the **initial creation** only. To later edit, close, comment,
or change labels/assignees, call ``update_github_issue``.

Args:
    owner: Repo owner login (user or org).
    repo: Repo name.
    title: Issue title (required, non-empty).
    body: Markdown body of the issue. Optional.
    labels: Comma-separated label names already defined in the repo,
        e.g. ``"bug,help wanted"``. Unknown labels will be silently
        ignored by GitHub.
    assignees: Comma-separated GitHub logins. The caller must have push
        access to the repo, and assignees themselves must be repo
        collaborators — GitHub silently drops invalid assignees.
    milestone: Numeric milestone id (not the title). Optional.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON of the new issue projected via ``_slim_issue_full``
    (number, title, state, body, labels, assignees, html_url, ...).

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: update_github_issue
description:
Apply a single mutation to an existing issue, dispatched by ``action``.

This tool intentionally aggregates 6 issue write endpoints under one tool
so the LLM picks an *intent* (close, comment, ...) instead of one of N
similarly-named tools. Each ``action`` consumes a specific subset of the
optional parameters; unrelated parameters are ignored.

Args:
    owner: Repo owner.
    repo: Repo name.
    number: Issue number.
    action: One of:
        - ``"edit"`` — uses ``title`` and/or ``body``. At least one required.
        - ``"close"`` — closes the issue. Optional ``state_reason``:
          ``"completed"`` (default) or ``"not_planned"``.
        - ``"reopen"`` — reopens the issue. No other params.
        - ``"comment"`` — adds a conversation comment. Requires
          ``comment_body``.
        - ``"set_labels"`` — **replaces the full label set**. ``labels``
          is a comma-separated list (empty string ``""`` clears all labels).
        - ``"set_assignees"`` — **replaces the full assignee set** by
          diffing against the current state. ``assignees`` is a
          comma-separated list of GitHub logins (empty string clears).
    title: For ``action="edit"``.
    body: For ``action="edit"``.
    state_reason: For ``action="close"``.
    comment_body: For ``action="comment"``.
    labels: For ``action="set_labels"``.
    assignees: For ``action="set_assignees"``.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the projected issue
    (or comment, for ``action="comment"``).

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: create_github_pull_request
description:
Open a new pull request.

Use this for the **initial creation** only. To later edit, close, comment,
add reviewers, or change labels/assignees, call ``update_github_pull_request``.
To approve / request changes / merge, call ``review_github_pull_request``.

Args:
    owner: Target repo owner.
    repo: Target repo name.
    title: PR title (required, non-empty).
    head: Source branch. For same-repo PRs use ``"feature-branch"``;
        for cross-fork PRs use ``"fork-owner:feature-branch"``.
    base: Target branch in the destination repo, e.g. ``"main"``.
    body: Markdown body. Optional.
    draft: Open as a draft PR. Defaults to ``False``.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON of the new PR projected via ``_slim_pull_request_full``.

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: update_github_pull_request
description:
Apply a single mutation to an existing pull request, dispatched by ``action``.

Mirrors ``update_github_issue`` plus a ``"set_reviewers"`` action.
Approve / request changes / merge are intentionally **not** here —
use ``review_github_pull_request`` for those (they are review events,
not property edits, and merge is destructive).

Args:
    owner: Repo owner.
    repo: Repo name.
    number: PR number.
    action: One of:
        - ``"edit"`` — uses ``title`` / ``body`` / ``base``. At least one required.
          ``base`` retargets the PR to a different branch.
        - ``"close"`` — closes the PR without merging. No other params.
        - ``"reopen"`` — reopens a closed PR. No other params.
        - ``"comment"`` — adds a conversation comment via the issues
          endpoint. Requires ``comment_body``.
        - ``"set_labels"`` — replaces the full label set. ``labels`` is
          comma-separated; empty string clears.
        - ``"set_assignees"`` — replaces the full assignee set
          (diff-and-apply). ``assignees`` comma-separated; empty clears.
        - ``"set_reviewers"`` — replaces requested reviewers
          (diff-and-apply). At least one of ``reviewers`` or
          ``team_reviewers`` must be provided; pass ``""`` for an
          already-supplied field to clear that side.
    title: For ``action="edit"``.
    body: For ``action="edit"``.
    base: For ``action="edit"``.
    comment_body: For ``action="comment"``.
    labels: For ``action="set_labels"``.
    assignees: For ``action="set_assignees"``.
    reviewers: For ``action="set_reviewers"``. Comma-separated user logins.
    team_reviewers: For ``action="set_reviewers"``. Comma-separated team
        slugs (org-only).
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the projected PR
    (or comment, for ``action="comment"``).

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: review_github_pull_request
description:
Submit a review event or merge a pull request.

These actions are kept apart from ``update_github_pull_request`` because
they are not property edits — a review is an immutable event in the PR
timeline, and a merge is destructive (cannot be undone via the API).

Args:
    owner: Repo owner.
    repo: Repo name.
    number: PR number.
    action: One of:
        - ``"approve"`` — submit an approving review. ``body`` optional.
        - ``"request_changes"`` — submit a changes-requested review.
          ``body`` is **required** by GitHub and validated here.
        - ``"comment"`` — submit a non-blocking review comment. ``body``
          is **required** when there are no ``line_comments``.
        - ``"merge"`` — merge the PR. Uses ``merge_method`` /
          ``commit_title`` / ``commit_message`` / ``sha``.
    body: Review body markdown. Semantics depend on ``action``; see above.
    line_comments: Optional line-level comments for the review, each
        shaped ``{"path": ..., "line": ..., "side": "RIGHT"|"LEFT",
        "body": ...}``. Only applies to review actions, not ``"merge"``.
    commit_id: Optional SHA the review should anchor to. Defaults to PR head.
    merge_method: For ``action="merge"``: ``"merge"`` (default) /
        ``"squash"`` / ``"rebase"``.
    commit_title: For ``action="merge"``. Optional.
    commit_message: For ``action="merge"``. Optional.
    sha: For ``action="merge"``. If set, GitHub rejects the merge unless
        the PR head still matches this SHA — defends against merging a
        stale branch.
    user_login: Leave empty to auto-detect the workspace credential.

Returns:
    Success — JSON containing the action taken plus the relevant payload
    (review object for review actions, merge result for merge).

    Failure — single-line error with action suggestion.

name: share_article_on_linkedin
description:
Share an external article/web link as a LinkedIn post.

WHEN TO CALL:
- The user wants to share a URL (blog post, news article, product page,
  GitHub repo, etc.) to LinkedIn with an optional commentary;
- The user explicitly asks to "post a link" / "share an article" on
  LinkedIn. For plain-text posts without any link, use
  `share_text_on_linkedin` instead.

REQUIRED OAUTH SCOPE: `w_member_social`.

Args:
    url: Required. The article / web URL to share. Must be a reachable
        http(s) URL.
    text: Optional. Commentary text shown above the link card.
    title: Optional. Title to display in the link card. If omitted,
        LinkedIn will try to scrape one from the page.
    description: Optional. Description to display in the link card.
    visibility: Optional. `"PUBLIC"` (default) or `"CONNECTIONS"`.
    linkedin_user_id: Optional. Same semantics as in
        `get_linkedin_user_info`.

Returns:
    On success — a Markdown confirmation plus a JSON payload with keys
    `post_id`, `visibility`, `shared_url`.
    On failure — a single-line reason plus an action suggestion.

Example:
    share_article_on_linkedin(
        url="https://openai.com/blog/xxx",
        text="Worth a read.",
        title="OpenAI Blog",
        description="Latest model release notes",
    )

name: composio_list_apps
description:
List the user's connected (authorized) apps on Composio platform.
Composio manages OAuth for apps like Instagram, and more.

Use this when the user asks about their Composio-connected apps specifically.
For a complete list of ALL connected connectors (including Google, GitHub, etc.),
use the `list_all_authorizations` tool instead.

name: composio_connect_app
description:
Initiate an OAuth connection via Composio platform.
Returns an authorization URL that the user should visit to complete the OAuth flow.

The enabled Composio apps are controlled by server config. By default,
only Instagram is enabled.

For Phoenix built-in connectors (Google, GitHub, Twitter, LinkedIn, Notion, TikTok, Square),
use the corresponding `start_<provider>_auth` tool instead (e.g. `start_google_auth`).

Instagram publishing guidance:
- Do not use browser automation first for Instagram posting. Browser Relay/CDP
  is not required for Accio-managed Composio Instagram tools.
- Before asking the user to authorize again, call COMPOSIO_CHECK_ACTIVE_CONNECTION
  with toolkit="instagram". If it returns ACTIVE, continue with Instagram MCP
  publish/media tools instead of opening Instagram in a browser.
- For Instagram tools that require ig_user_id, use "me" unless the user
  provided a specific Instagram Business Account ID. Do not use Composio
  connected_account_id values such as "ca_*" as ig_user_id.
- Only call this tool when no ACTIVE Instagram connection exists or when the
  user explicitly asks to reconnect / re-authorize.

Args:
    app_name: The name of the app to connect, e.g. "instagram" or "ins".
    intent: Reserved for desktop client use; do not set this argument from a
        language model. The default 'auto' is idempotent — when the user
        already has a healthy ACTIVE connection it is reused without asking
        the user to authorize again.
